Subject: Post-demo recap — private connectivity, auth & routing (next steps)

Hi Arjun / Megan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so your team can evaluate how Redwood will fit into EdgeWave's air-gapped VPC topology. I focused this summary on the integration topics you flagged: SDK setup, auth, routing, structured output/tool-calling, and networking (VPC endpoints, IP allowlists, egress, DNS, mTLS).

Key points I captured: 
- Requirement: No outbound public internet from inference hosts — traffic must go via a VPC endpoint to Redwood Private.
- Auth: Service-to-service token flow (short-lived JWTs) with customer-managed KMS for key wrapping.
- DNS: Internal DNS resolution to our VPC endpoint (we can provide a CNAME for your internal zone).
- mTLS: Mutual TLS supported for control plane and optional data-plane tunnels.
- Embeddings / Reranker: Bulk embedding uploads will go over the endpoint; reranker calls are standard API requests (we recommend batch rerankers for throughput).

Proposed next steps: 
1) Action: We’ll share a concise connectivity checklist and a sample SDK auth snippet for your infra team to validate NAT/firewall rules (attached).
2) Action: Engineering sync — can we book a 30-min technical handoff with your infra and security folks (Arjun + whoever owns KMS)?
3) Action: Ben (cc'd) will follow up on commercial terms and estimated capacity so we can map Dedicated capacity vs Private deployment.

Attachments: private_connectivity_checklist.pdf (networking checklist), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (proposed timeline).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the eng sync for Thu or Fri — what time windows work for you?

Thanks,
Soojin

Thanks Soojin — very helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: All inference traffic must traverse a VPC interface endpoint (no public egress). We also need an allowlist for the endpoint IPs at our perimeter.
- DNS: We run an internal private zone (Route53) — we prefer a CNAME mapping your endpoint to an internal hostname.
- mTLS: Security requires mTLS for control-plane API calls; optional for data-plane. Can you confirm supported cipher suites and rotation cadence?
- KMS: We use AWS KMS with a customer-managed CMK and need proof of key-wrapping interactions (audit logs).
- Throughput: Initial POC will be ~20 rps for embeddings and 15 rps for generation; please confirm batching recommendations.

Can you send: 
- Example VPC endpoint config (subnet/NACL/route table guidance)
- Sample SDK auth flow (JWT exchange) and a minimal TLS config we can load-test in a lab
- Any compliance artifacts for KMS usage we can share with our security team

We can do an eng sync Thu 3/22 10:00–10:30 PT — Arjun + our infra lead + security.

—Arjun

Arjun — quick deliverables from us (scope & links) before the eng sync: 

1) VPC endpoint example (copy/paste):
- Create Interface Endpoint in your VPC: service: com.redwood.private.v1, subnets: app-subnet-1/app-subnet-2
- Security groups: allow outbound 443 to Redwood managed IPs (we supply IPs via allowlist)
- Route tables: no special routes required for interface endpoints

2) SDK auth snippet (short-lived JWT exchange):
- Step A: EdgeWave infra generates a signed short-lived JWT using your CMK (expires 5m)
- Step B: POST /v1/auth/exchange (mutual TLS) with signed_jwt -> returns transient bearer token (1h)

Sample cURL (replace placeholders):
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key -X POST https://private.redwood.example.com/v1/auth/exchange -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"signed_jwt":"<BASE64_JWT>"}'

3) mTLS notes: we support mutual TLS with RSA/ECDSA certs. We rotate server certs quarterly; client cert rotation per customer policy. Supported TLS versions: 1.2/1.3. Cipher suites: ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256.

4) Batching guidance (Jonas attached will expand):
- Embeddings: batch up to 128 items per request for best throughput; prefer 512-d vectors split into chunks for indexing pipelines.
- Reranker: send candidate sets of up to 64 per request; consider client-side pre-filtering for latency-sensitive paths.

5) Compliance artifacts: I’ve attached summary docs; for KMS audit logs we can provide redacted examples and our audit integration guide.

Related links: hubspot (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8055/EW-2028-197) and a short tech doc: https://docs.redwood.com/sdk/auth#vpc-endpoint-example

If that looks good I’ll leave the calendar invite for Thu 3/22 10:00 PT and we’ll share a short meeting agenda.

Soojin
